work_arrangement.t: For a married couple with young children, both parents working full time and sharing childcare is usually best.
means: Two full-time jobs plus shared childcare or daycare beats having a parent at home

work_arrangement.t: Both parents working, with one part time, is usually best.
means: One parent cuts back hours while children are young, but neither stops working

work_arrangement.t: One parent staying home while the children are young is usually best.
means: Even when two incomes are affordable, a parent at home full time is better for young children

caregiver_parent.t: Which parent stays home should depend on who wants to or who earns less, not on sex.
means: A father staying home is just as good as a mother doing it

caregiver_parent.t: Usually the mother should stay home, but either is fine.
means: Mothers are a slightly better default, though fathers can do it well

caregiver_parent.t: The mother should stay home; young children need their mother.
means: A father at home isn't an equal substitute for a mother at home

marriage_decisions.t: Major family decisions should be made equally by both spouses.
means: Neither spouse gets the final say on where to live or big spending

marriage_decisions.t: Major decisions are equal, but each spouse leads in different areas.
means: Spouses divide up who takes the lead on, say, money, the house or the children

marriage_decisions.t: The husband should have the final say on major family decisions.
means: When spouses disagree on where to live or big spending, the husband decides

promote_marriage.t: Government shouldn't favor married people over unmarried people.
yes: Treating married and unmarried people alike in taxes and benefits

promote_marriage.t: Government should only remove tax and benefit rules that penalize marriage.
yes: Fixing marriage penalties in taxes and aid
Bonuses or tax breaks for married couples
Public campaigns promoting marriage
no: Treating marriage as a private matter

unmarried_partner_rights.t: Unmarried couples who live together should have the same legal rights as married couples.
yes: Inheritance, hospital visits and similar rights for cohabiting couples

unmarried_partner_rights.t: Unmarried couples should get some rights after living together several years.
yes: Limited rights after years together

unmarried_partner_rights.t: Those rights should come with marriage.
yes: Reserving inheritance and hospital rights for married couples

childcare_spending.t: Government should make childcare free for every family with children under 5.
yes: Free childcare for all families, whatever their income

childcare_spending.t: No family should pay more than about 7% of its income for childcare.
yes: Subsidies capping childcare costs at about 7% of income

childcare_spending.t: Childcare help should go to low-income families only, as today.
yes: Today's subsidies for low-income families

childcare_spending.t: No government help with childcare costs.
yes: Ending childcare subsidies

childcare_form.t: Help for families with young children should go mainly to childcare programs, so parents can work.
yes: Funding daycare and preschool programs
no: Cash to parents as the main form of help

childcare_form.t: Help should be split between childcare programs and cash to parents.
yes: Both childcare funding and cash payments
no: Putting it all into one or the other

childcare_form.t: Help should go mainly to parents as cash, whether they use childcare or stay home.
yes: Cash payments that parents spend as they choose

stay_home_support.t: Support should go to childcare so parents can work, not to parents who stay home.
yes: Childcare subsidies for working parents

stay_home_support.t: Some support for both, but more for childcare.
yes: Larger childcare subsidies plus some help for stay-at-home parents

stay_home_support.t: Parents who stay home should get the same support as parents who pay for childcare.
yes: Equal credits or payments either way

no_fault_divorce.t: One spouse should be able to divorce without the other's agreement or proof of wrongdoing, as today.
yes: Keeping no-fault divorce

no_fault_divorce.t: Keep no-fault divorce, but with a longer waiting period when there are children.
yes: Longer waiting periods for parents

no_fault_divorce.t: Divorce should require agreement or proof of fault, like abuse or adultery.
yes: Ending no-fault divorce
no: Divorce over one spouse's objection without fault

pay_transparency.t: Large employers should post pay ranges and report pay by gender.
yes: Pay ranges in job ads
Reporting pay by gender to the government

pay_transparency.t: Large employers should post pay ranges only.
yes: Pay ranges in job ads

pay_transparency.t: Neither: no pay posting or reporting rules.
yes: Leaving pay disclosure to employers

board_gender_rules.t: Large public companies should have at least 40% women on their boards.
yes: A legal minimum of 40% women on boards

board_gender_rules.t: No board quota, but companies must report how many women serve.
yes: Required reporting of board gender

board_gender_rules.t: No board gender requirement or reporting.
yes: Leaving board makeup to shareholders

birth_rate_policy.t: Birth rates are a personal choice, not a government concern.
yes: No policies aimed at birth rates

birth_rate_policy.t: Make raising children more affordable, but don't aim at raising birth rates.
yes: Help with child costs for families who have children
no: Payments designed to get people to have more children

birth_rate_policy.t: Government should aim to raise birth rates with large payments or tax breaks for each child.
yes: Large baby bonuses or tax breaks per child
no: Treating birth rates as none of government's business

workplace_gender_programs.t: Large employers should run programs to bring more women into jobs where they're few, with hiring targets and required training.
yes: Hiring targets for women
Required training

workplace_gender_programs.t: Large employers should run outreach and mentoring for women, without targets.
yes: Recruiting and mentoring programs for women

workplace_gender_programs.t: Large employers should run only general training on treating everyone equally.
yes: Equal-treatment training for all

workplace_gender_programs.t: No such programs, but leave the choice to each company.
yes: Letting companies decide

workplace_gender_programs.t: No such programs, and government should bar them at federal contractors.
yes: Barring gender-targeted programs at companies with federal contracts
no: Programs aimed at hiring or promoting women

women_draft.t: If there's a draft, women should be drafted on the same terms as men.
yes: Women registering and serving in any role, including combat

women_draft.t: Women should be drafted, but only for non-combat roles.
yes: Drafting women for support roles
Keeping draft registration for men only

natural_roles.t: Differences in men's and women's family roles come almost entirely from upbringing and culture.
means: If children were raised differently, mothers and fathers would take on the same roles

natural_roles.t: They come mostly from culture, partly from nature.
means: Biology plays a small part, but upbringing explains most of the difference

natural_roles.t: They come about equally from culture and nature.
means: Upbringing and biology matter about the same

natural_roles.t: They come mostly from natural differences between the sexes.
means: Biology explains most of why mothers and fathers take on different roles

natural_roles.t: They come almost entirely from nature; men and women are suited to different roles.
means: Mothers and fathers take different roles mainly because of biology, not upbringing
